bug_semantics: Yggdrasil exports com.redhat.Yggdrasil1.Dispatch() on the system bus and forwards the caller's directive, message id, metadata, and payload to a named worker (including package-manager workers that can add repos and install/remove RPMs). The installed D-Bus busconfig used <policy context="default"> with <allow send_destination="com.redhat.Yggdrasil1"/>, so any local uid could send to that destination, and Dispatch itself took no dbus.Sender argument and performed no uid/authorization check (unlike Dispatcher.Transmit). A local unprivileged user could therefore force a privileged worker to install arbitrary packages, yielding LPE (CWE-280).

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2025-3931 / GHSA-rpg2-jvhp-h354 is a live published Red Hat CNA record (not withdrawn/rejected). The sink is local unauthenticated invocation of com.redhat.Yggdrasil1.Dispatch on the system bus, which relays arbitrary content to workers; a package-manager worker running privileged then yields LPE. The code-level hole is the conjunction of (1) a D-Bus method that does not inspect the sender and (2) a busconfig default policy that allows every uid to send to com.redhat.Yggdrasil1. The shipped fix 196d0cbea42f72e6dfecaa563681a99e9fdb4a38 only tightens (2) to user="root", which is sufficient on the system bus because unmatched send is denied.
